motion.value: opacity 0→1, scale 0.98→1, origin = edge facing the selection; duration-base, ease-out

motion.name: reduced-motion

focus.fallback: If the injected OS accent is below 3:1 against the surface, --color-focus-ring resolves to --color-text-primary.

materials.fallback: Windows 10, transparency off, reduce transparency, or helper unavailable: solid surfaces (surface-popup-solid etc.), signalled by :root[data-material="none"]. Windows 10 popups are also square (rounded.popup-win10 = 0).

platform.selector: :root[data-os="macos" | "windows"] set by the shell; Windows 10 adds data-os-version="10" (square popups). data-material="native" | "none" chooses veil or solid surfaces.

picker.loupe: 120px rounded square (rounded.popup), 15x15 device px at 8x8 CSS px each, 1px grid in picker-halo at 25%, centre cell outlined; no caption.
picker.snapCandidate: Cuts a scrim hole and draws the selection stroke at 60% opacity.
picker.hintBar: Top centre of the work area, 16px in; jumps (no animation) to the bottom when the pointer or selection is within 48px. Adds the egress pill (dark-appearance colours) for cloud pipelines.
picker.handles: 8px squares, picker-stroke fill, 1px picker-halo ring, rounded.box; 20px hit area; edge midpoints hidden on edges under 48px.
picker.cancel: Esc or right-click, from any phase.

snip.structure: Block list (scrolls; skipped line is its last item) then a 24px footer: provider indicator, Private mark, status, then Show original / Copy / Close icon buttons. No header.
snip.placement: GAP 8, MARGIN 8, width clamp(region, 280, 480); below if >= 200 (COMFORT_H), above, inline-end / inline-start if >= 280, larger of below/above if >= 96 (MIN_H), else inside the region's block-end inline-end corner. Below/above align inline-start edges.
snip.languageTags: Only when the region has two or more source languages, or Settings says always; always in the skipped expansion.
snip.packRows: One row per missing language at the top of the list.
snip.dismiss: Esc, Close, or click outside (consumed by the picker overlays).

live.structure: 28px strip (dot, label, local indicator; Private, pause/resume, re-pin, stop; no Hide), then a 24px cloud row while cloud is in use, then a state row, then the block list. No footer.
live.docking: Side fixed at pin time. Below/above: centred, width clamp(region, 240, 640). Sides: width clamp(space, 240, 400). Thresholds 160 (comfort), 240 (side), 80 (min). Not draggable.
live.blockPadding: 4px 8px 4px 20px on every Live block; change mark 6px at inline-start 8px, centred on the first line.
live.settling: Nothing greys out while pixels settle; 'Updating' only after 1000ms of processing.
live.stale: Paused/error: hollow or danger dot, blocks in text-secondary, body state row 'Showing text from {age}'. heading type only for error and consent titles.
live.frame: Native click-through corner ticks outside the region; region tag only while the popup is hidden.

narrative.overview:
Glimpse writes the meaning of foreign text in the margin beside it, the way a reader pencils a gloss next to a hard line. The note is small, plain and close to its source. It never covers the original, it never decorates itself, and it disappears when the page is turned. Every surface (the region picker, the Snip popup, the Live docked popup, settings, onboarding, the tray item) is the same quiet hand: system type, the OS's own materials and accent, neutral tints, and colour used only to say something.

Density is that of a native utility, not a product page. Popups are compact and content-first: the translation is the largest thing on the surface, controls are small and secondary, and there is no header art, no logo and no empty decoration. Settings and onboarding follow the host OS's settings conventions (grouped rows, standard controls, sidebar or stepped layout) so a Windows user and a Mac user each recognise them at once. The world contributes type, palette and one signature move only; it never supplies controls or layout.

The signature move is the **linked gloss**: hovering or focusing a block in the popup lights its detected box on screen, and in Live mode a block that just changed carries a brief tint that settles into a faint resting mark. Source and meaning are always visibly connected, and change is shown, not churned.
keyCharacteristics: System UI fonts on each OS, with per-script Noto fallbacks; no web fonts, no display face.
Neutral, untinted greys that read as OS chrome; the OS accent drives interactive colour.
Native window materials (macOS vibrancy, Windows Acrylic/Mica) under a tint that guarantees legibility over any screen content.
Colour carries state only: accent for action, focus and linkage; violet for cloud egress; standard status hues.
Motion is fast, short and explanatory; Live mode never animates anything that did not change.
Logical (direction-agnostic) layout everywhere; RTL and mixed-direction text are first-class.

rules.name: The Ninety Rule
rules.body: Any translucent surface that carries secondary text or body copy is at least 90% opaque. That is the floor at which every text token still passes 4.5:1 when the content behind the window is pure white or pure black. Lower opacity is allowed only for surfaces that carry primary text and headings alone (`surface-window`, 72%).

rules.name: The Borrowed Accent Rule
rules.body: Glimpse has no brand colour in its UI. Interactive colour is the user's OS accent; the app-icon orange stays in the icon, the installer and the README.

rules.name: The Violet Means Leaving Rule
rules.body: Egress violet appears if and only if data left, or will leave, the device. Never use it for decoration, promotion or "premium" cues.

rules.name: The No Costume Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels, no letter-spacing tweaks, no condensed or display faces, no monospace outside literal data. They fail in half the scripts Glimpse renders, and the OS never uses them.

rules.name: The Leading Follows Script Rule
rules.body: Line height is set per script, not per surface. A token's line height is the Latin value; the script table overrides it.

rules.name: The Borrowed Depth Rule
rules.body: The window is the only elevated object. Inside a popup everything is flat: no cards, no shadows, no nested surfaces. Groups are separated by space and dividers.

dos: **Do** paint `surface-popup` (90% opaque) over the native material and switch to `surface-popup-solid` when the OS asks for less transparency.
**Do** take interactive colour from the OS accent, with the frontmatter hex as the fallback only.
**Do** tag every rendered block with its detected `lang` and `dir="auto"`, and let `:lang()` choose stack and leading.
**Do** use logical properties for every inline-axis value.
**Do** keep each popup flat: blocks separated by 8px and, where needed, a `divider`.
**Do** show the cloud-in-use indicator with icon and provider name on every cloud-handled result and in the tray.
**Do** honour reduced motion by removing movement while keeping the change tint, mark and text updates.
donts: **Don't** use gradients, gradient text, glows, coloured shadows or CSS glassmorphism; the only glass is the OS material.
**Don't** add cards, nested surfaces, eyebrows or kicker labels above headings, section numbers, or hero blocks to any surface.
**Don't** use uppercase or tracked labels, display faces, or monospace as decoration.
**Don't** mark changed Live blocks with a coloured side stripe, a border thicker than 1px, a pulsing dot or a shake.
**Don't** use spinners or shimmer inside content; show the real source text, then the translation.
**Don't** use the app-icon orange (#EA580C) anywhere in the UI.
**Don't** use egress violet for anything except data leaving the device, and never rely on colour alone for it.
**Don't** use emoji or Unicode glyphs as icons, celebration states, confetti or mascots.
**Don't** animate a whole popup, or any unchanged block, when Live content updates.
**Don't** let any Glimpse surface cover the selected or pinned region.
